title.narrative: Implementation of SDGs in Ukraine in the context of recovery from the war and towards the European integration

description.narrative: Since February 2022 Ukraine has been focusing on addressing the challenges caused by Russia’s full-scale invasion. The ongoing full-fledged war is keeping the needs of the people of Ukraine, their safety and security on top of the agenda, and simultaneously brings new priorities, developments, and aspects of the national policies of the country. Just before the war started, Ukraine had been making steady progress in achieving 15 of the 17 SDGs. However, projections made by UNDP suggest that up to 90 percent of the population of Ukraine could face poverty and vulnerability to poverty if the war continues. Furthermore, women have been disproportionally affected by the war, accounting for more than half of the Internally Displaced People and of those needing humanitarian assistance in 2024. UNDP has been supporting the Government of Ukraine (GoU) in implementing several reforms that catalyse Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) attainment, including those related to democratic (transparent and accountable) governance, sustainable environment and energy efficiency, and in the past two years also addressing the far-reaching consequences of the escalated war. Additionally, following the European Councils decision to open accession negotiations with Ukraine on 14 December 2023, the Ukrainian Government initiated an active phase of preparations for Ukraines accession to the European Union. This process has concurrently contributed to Ukraines progress towards the SDGs, demonstrating how the European integration efforts can complement and enhance national development strategies aimed at achieving a sustainable future. In this context, it is of tremendous importance not to lose all the progress Ukraine has achieved in sustainable development and ensuring the efforts towards achievement of the SDGs constitute the backbone of Ukraine’s recovery processes as well as strong basis for the European integration.
